tasks.subject: Task 2: Scanner sees block and trailing comments
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `comment_scan.py` recognises comment text that is not a line-leading `//`, without a lexer and without any path that can read code as a comment.

**Files:**
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan.py`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/guard-evals.json`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh:155`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ` * ABC-1234: the inbound HELP keyword.` is scanned as comment text (no tell matches it without a configured pattern, but the text reaches `TELLS`)
- [ ] ` * Fixes #123` is flagged as an issue reference
- [ ] `/* fixes task-42 */` is flagged
- [ ] `val x = 1 // fixes task-42` is flagged
- [ ] `*p = task-42;` is NOT flagged - `*` opens a comment only when followed by whitespace or end-of-line
- [ ] `x = "a" + "b//c"` is NOT flagged even with a tell inside the string
- [ ] `echo "a #b"` in a `.sh` file is NOT flagged
- [ ] `url=${url#https://t/task-42}` in a `.sh` file is NOT flagged
- [ ] Every pre-existing eval case still passes

**Verify:** `bash plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh` -> all 100 cases pass

Adds `comment_text`, `_trailing_comment` and `_quotes_balanced`; extends `DEFAULT_COMMENT` to `("//", "/*", "*/", "*")` with `*/` before `*`. The parity test declines any line where an odd count of unescaped quotes precedes the delimiter - it can miss a comment but never promote code to comment. Full code for all three functions is in the plan document under "Task 2".

Also run `bash plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-report.sh` - a new false positive means a defect in the parity test, not an acceptable cost.


tasks.subject: Task 3: Project ticket pattern with a scan deadline
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A project can name its tracker-key shape and have the scanner enforce it, with no default and no way for a bad pattern to hang a blocking hook.

**Files:**
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan.py`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/guard-evals.json`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh:155`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-scan.py`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-report.sh`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] With `ANTI_TANGENT_TICKET_PATTERN='ABC-\d+'`, `// ABC-1234: the keyword` is flagged as a tracker reference
- [ ] With the variable unset, the same line is clean
- [ ] A pattern that fails to compile is ignored, and the scanner still runs its other tells
- [ ] A pattern longer than 200 characters is ignored
- [ ] A catastrophic-backtracking pattern causes the scan to return no violations rather than hanging
- [ ] `fp-scan.py` and `fp-report.sh` unset the variable so the false-positive gate does not depend on the developer's environment

**Verify:** `bash plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh` -> all 103 cases pass

There is deliberately NO default pattern - a generic `[A-Z]+-\d+` matches `HDMI-0`, `DP-0`, `ROUND-1` far more often than tracker keys, and this hook blocks writes. The ReDoS guard is a `signal.setitimer` deadline, not a structural nested-quantifier check: that check misses `(a|aa)+` and `(a|a)*`, and `(a+)+$` over a 40-character line still hangs. Full code is in the plan document under "Task 3". `run.sh` already supports per-case `"env"` (line 398) - no harness change needed.

```json:metadata
{"files": ["plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan.py", "plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/guard-evals.json", "plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh", "plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-scan.py", "plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-report.sh"], "verifyCommand": "bash plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh && bash plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-report.sh", "acceptanceCriteria": ["a configured pattern flags a tracker key", "unset means no ticket tell at all", "an uncompilable pattern is dropped without disabling other tells", "an over-long pattern is refused", "a backtracking pattern trips the deadline and fails open", "the FP gate unsets the variable"], "modelTier": "mechanical"}
```

tasks.subject: Task 4: Separate the two close-time kill switches
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `ANTI_TANGENT_COMPLETION_GUARD=0` disables the completion gate and nothing else; `ANTI_TANGENT_COMMENT_GUARD=0` disables comment scanning and nothing else.

**Files:**
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/check-task-complete`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/guard-evals.json`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh:155`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `COMPLETION_GUARD=0`, `COMMENT_GUARD=1`, a close carrying a bad comment -> exit 2 on comment hygiene
- [ ] `COMPLETION_GUARD=0`, `COMMENT_GUARD=1`, a close with no validate_completion at all -> exit 0
- [ ] `COMPLETION_GUARD=1`, `COMMENT_GUARD=0`, a close with no validate_completion -> exit 2
- [ ] Both `0` -> exit 0 with a `skip` trace
- [ ] The comment-block message no longer claims "the completion gate passed"

**Verify:** `bash plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh` -> all 107 cases pass

The current early exit at `check-task-complete:170` returns above the `COMMENT_GUARD` read at 174. The fix reads both variables up front, exits early only when both are `0`, and hoists the comment-hygiene block above the completion logic so it runs independent of the verdict. Full replacement bash and all four eval cases (with complete transcripts) are in the plan document under "Task 4".

Note: this is a documented behaviour reversal - `CLAUDE.md` currently says `COMPLETION_GUARD=0` "silences the whole close-time hook". Task 10 updates the docs; do not update them here.

tasks.subject: Task 5: Scan final_files completions using git
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A lightweight completion that submits full file contents instead of a diff is no longer unscanned, without ever flagging a comment the implementer did not add.

**Files:**
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/check-task-complete`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/guard-evals.json`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh:155`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A `final_files` completion naming an untracked file whose content carries `// fixes #1` blocks the close
- [ ] A `final_files` completion naming a tracked file whose pre-existing comment carries `// fixes #1`, with no modification, does NOT block
- [ ] A path inside a nested git worktree resolves against that worktree, not the hook's cwd
- [ ] A gitignored path is skipped
- [ ] A path outside any repository is skipped
- [ ] `final_diff` still wins when both fields are present
- [ ] Git is invoked with diff prefixes pinned, so a user's `diff.mnemonicPrefix` or `diff.noprefix` cannot blind the parser

**Verify:** `bash plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh` -> all 110 cases pass

THE CRITICAL DETAIL: every git call is rooted at the file's OWN directory via `git -C "$(dirname "$path")"`. From the main checkout, `git ls-files --error-unmatch <path inside a nested worktree>` exits 1 - indistinguishable from untracked - which would scan the whole file and block on comments nobody added. This is reproduced in Step 4 of the plan; run it before trusting the evals. Exit 1 means unmatched; anything else (128 = outside a repo, or no HEAD) means skip.

This task also adds a `setup_script` hook to `run.sh` (the harness has none, and `tmpdir_fixture` can only place file content, not build a git repo). Full code for `_git`, `final_files_added_lines`, the harness hook, and all three eval cases is in the plan document under "Task 5".


tasks.subject: Task 7: Flatten the CodeScene ladder to one rung
tasks.description:
**Goal:** Under `ANTI_TANGENT_CODESCENE=required`, inventing a skip reason stops being cheaper than staying silent, and the resulting finding routes the implementer to attach evidence rather than to rework code.

**Files:**
- Modify: `internal/mcpsrv/submission_defect.go`
- Modify: `internal/planrun/report.go:85-98`
- Test: `internal/mcpsrv/handlers_test.go`
- Test: `internal/planrun/report_test.go`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Mode unset -> no adoption finding for any digest shape
- [ ] `required`, no `codescene` argument -> major `codescene_not_run`
- [ ] `required`, `ran:false`, empty `skip_reason` -> major `codescene_not_run`
- [ ] `required`, `ran:false`, `skip_reason:"lightweight task"`, no evidence -> major `codescene_skipped`
- [ ] `required`, `ran:false`, any reason plus non-empty `skip_evidence` -> minor `codescene_skipped`
- [ ] `required`, `ran:true` -> no adoption finding; a regression still yields its own minor
- [ ] `CategoryCodesceneSkipped` is in `submissionDefectCategories`, so an envelope blocked only by the new major reports `SubmissionDefectOnly` and gets the re-submit next_action
- [ ] The minor's suggestion no longer claims the skip is recorded in the plan-run ledger
- [ ] `codesceneCell` renders the evidence alongside the reason

**Verify:** `go test -race ./internal/mcpsrv/... ./internal/planrun/...` -> PASS

The ladder becomes one rung: a reason with no evidence is graded EXACTLY as silence. That is what removes the incentive - with both equal there is nothing left to buy by inventing a sentence. No keyword classification of reasons; "lightweight task" draws a major because it carries no evidence, not because a list names it. The ledger-promise fix matters because `handlers.go:1711` gates the write on `!lightweight`, so on the lightweight path nothing is recorded and the old suggestion text was false.

Existing tests asserting minor-for-any-reason WILL fail - update them to supply `skip_evidence`; the behaviour change is the point. Full code and both tests are in the plan document under "Task 7".

```json:metadata
{"files": ["internal/mcpsrv/submission_defect.go", "internal/mcpsrv/handlers_test.go", "internal/planrun/report.go", "internal/planrun/report_test.go"], "verifyCommand": "go test -race ./internal/mcpsrv/... ./internal/planrun/...", "acceptanceCriteria": ["unset mode emits no adoption finding", "an unevidenced skip is a major", "an evidenced skip is a minor", "codescene_skipped is submission-defect-only", "the ledger promise is removed from the suggestion", "codesceneCell renders skip evidence"], "modelTier": "standard"}
```

tasks.subject: Task 8: Reject test evidence showing nothing ran
tasks.description:
**Goal:** `validate_completion` stops accepting output which states that no test executed, without penalising a cached run that attests a prior pass.

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/mcpsrv/test_evidence.go`
- Create: `internal/mcpsrv/test_evidence_test.go`
- Modify: `internal/mcpsrv/handlers.go:1688`
- Modify: `internal/prompts/templates/post.tmpl`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `:app:test NO-SOURCE` yields one major `insufficient_evidence` with criterion `test_evidence`
- [ ] pytest's `no tests ran`, jest's `No tests found`, and Go's `?   pkg   [no test files]` each yield the same finding
- [ ] `:app:test UP-TO-DATE`, `:app:test FROM-CACHE` and `ok  pkg  0.01s (cached)` yield nothing
- [ ] A Gradle log with several `UP-TO-DATE` compile tasks and one executed test task yields nothing
- [ ] A human-written summary ("all 4 tests pass") yields nothing
- [ ] Empty `test_evidence` yields nothing
- [ ] The finding is submission-defect-only, so `next_action` tells the implementer to re-submit
- [ ] `post.tmpl` tells the reviewer not to restate this finding

**Verify:** `go test -race ./internal/mcpsrv/... ./internal/prompts/...` -> PASS

THE PREMISE THAT GOVERNS THIS TASK: Gradle marks a task `UP-TO-DATE`/`FROM-CACHE` only after a SUCCESSFUL prior execution on unchanged inputs (a failing test task re-executes), and `go test` caches only passing results. Those markers therefore attest that the tests pass - they carry no counts, but neither does a plain successful Gradle run. Firing on them would penalise the cached run and accept an equally count-free executed one. Only markers meaning "nothing ran" fire. Write the NEGATIVE tests first; they are the ones that encode this.

Full code for `testEvidenceFindings`, both marker lists, the handler wiring and the `post.tmpl` sentence are in the plan document under "Task 8". Step 7 regenerates goldens - read the diff, only `post_*` goldens with a test-evidence section should move.


The consolidation matters: `FinalizePlanVerdict` turns three minors into a `warn`, so one finding per fence would push a plan with three tracker-key comments to `warn` on count alone. `RenderPlan(in PlanInput) (Output, error)` is the real signature (`prompts.go:416`); `Output` has `System` and `User`. `plan_rules` is shared by all three plan templates, which is why all twelve goldens move. Full section text and test are in the plan document under "Task 9".
